title: Prove what works: a fair trial, a field day and your 90-day plan
course_title: Sustainable Agriculture Practices: Healthy Soil, Smart Water and Climate-Ready Farming

say: Prove what works: a fair trial, a field day, and your 90-day plan.
This is the video for Module 3 of Sustainable Agriculture Practices.
Rainfall is getting harder to predict. Climate-smart farming helps you produce more and recover from shocks. Ask your ADP which certified drought-tolerant or early-maturing varieties suit your zone.

say: A neighbour says her mulched maize did better. But was it the mulch, or did she also plant earlier and use a new variety? A fair trial tells you what works on your land. Step one. Choose one change, for example mulch or no mulch.

panel.heading: Running a fair side-by-side trial
items: Mark two equal plots, side by side

say: Step two. Mark two plots of the same size on similar soil, for example 10 m by 10 m each, with pegs and string.

panel.heading: Running a fair side-by-side trial
items: Mark two equal plots, side by side

say: Step three. Treat both exactly the same, except the one practice you are testing.

panel.heading: Running a fair side-by-side trial
items: Mark two equal plots, side by side
panel.rule: Change one thing only. Keep everything else the same.

say: Step four. Label the plots and write the plan in your notebook before planting.

say: Steps five and six. Note crop height, wilting and pests every week. Then harvest and weigh each plot separately, and compare per square metre.

say: The mulched plot gave 52 kg of dry grain. The unmulched plot gave 40 kg. That is 0.52 against 0.40 kg per square metre, 30 percent more.
At about 700 naira per kg, the extra 12 kg is worth 8,400 naira.

say: Collecting and spreading mulch took 1 day, valued at about 3,000 naira.

say: So her net gain on 100 square metres is about 5,400 naira. Because one season can mislead, she will repeat the trial next year.
And be honest. If a plot is spoilt by goats or late weeding, record it, and never stretch one good result into a promise to neighbours.

say: Your state ADP, NAERLS, research institutes like IITA, and farmer groups can all help. But extension officers cover many farmers, and a vague request is easy to forget.

panel.heading: Ask your extension officer well
right: Water took over an hour to soak in
Maize wilts after a week dry

say: Use your own numbers. My sandy loam took over an hour to absorb water, and my maize wilts after one week without rain. Can you advise a drought-tolerant variety and visit my trial in July? Send it with a photo, and follow up politely.

say: Farmers trust what they see on a neighbour's farm. For example, Ngozi near Awka invited 15 women to her compost and mulch plots on a Saturday after market. Water, snacks and picture sheets cost about 9,000 naira. Start with a welcome and the problem.
Walk the two plots, so people see the difference.
Share your numbers.
Then let everyone try it. Ngozi's group built a small compost heap together.
End with questions. Collect names and numbers only with permission, and keep the list safe. And never call produce organic unless you can show it.

panel.rule: Ask before adding anyone to a group or sharing their photo.

say: Your capstone is an evidence pack: baseline, practices, trial records, results, lessons and a plan. Track the same indicators each year. Yield per square metre and harvest per bag of fertiliser should rise.

panel.heading: Indicators to track every season
items: Water intake time at the same spots
Earthworm count, same spots and month
Days the crop survives a dry spell

say: Water should soak in faster, and you should find more earthworms.

say: Sprays should fall, and your crop should survive dry spells longer. Grace in Jos found her mulched maize gave about 22 percent more, and honestly noted a compost heap that stayed cold.

say: Break your plan into three months. Days 1 to 30, prepare.

Hold a field day or group visit, and review your records against the indicators.

say: To remember. Spread your climate risk. Test one change at a time. Compare per square metre and net gain. Ask for help with your own numbers. And record results honestly, then repeat.

say: Now design your trial and photograph both plots on planting day. Write one specific request to your extension officer and plan a field day. Then draft your one-page project summary with a dated 90-day plan.
